knowledge_base.title: NICU — Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
knowledge_base.content: NICU stands for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. It provides care for premature or critically ill newborns. Common terms include corrected gestational age (CGA), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). NICU patients may require mechanical ventilation, total parenteral nutrition (TPN), and phototherapy.

knowledge_base.title: CVICU — Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit
knowledge_base.content: CVICU stands for Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit. It handles post-cardiac surgery and severe cardiac conditions. Key terms: coronary artery bypass graft (CABG), intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), left ventricular assist device (LVAD), atrial fibrillation (AFib), ejection fraction (EF), and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP).

knowledge_base.title: PICU — Pediatric Intensive Care Unit
knowledge_base.content: PICU stands for Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. It cares for critically ill children. Common terms include respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), status epilepticus (SE), diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), septic shock, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Sedation protocols and weight-based dosing are standard.

knowledge_base.title: ICU — Intensive Care Unit
knowledge_base.content: ICU stands for Intensive Care Unit. General critical care terminology includes mean arterial pressure (MAP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2), sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA), central venous pressure (CVP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine clearance (CrCl), and vasopressors such as norepinephrine.

knowledge_base.title: HUC — Health Unit Coordinator
knowledge_base.content: HUC stands for Health Unit Coordinator (also called unit clerk or ward clerk). Responsibilities include managing physician orders, coordinating admissions, discharges and transfers (ADT), maintaining medical records (MR), processing lab requisitions, and communicating with nursing staff. HUC works closely with the charge nurse and handles EMR (Electronic Medical Records) entry.

knowledge_base.title: ED — Emergency Department
knowledge_base.content: ED stands for Emergency Department. Key acronyms include triage levels (ESI 1–5), chief complaint (CC), history of present illness (HPI), mechanism of injury (MOI), point-of-care testing (POCT), rapid sequence intubation (RSI), emergency medical technician (EMT), and trauma activation. STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) and stroke codes are time-critical ED events.

knowledge_base.title: NICU — Respiratory Support Terminology
knowledge_base.content: NICU respiratory support includes high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), nasal intermittent positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV), and surfactant replacement therapy. Oxygen saturation targets (SpO2) are typically 91–95% in premature infants. Apnea of prematurity (AOP) is treated with caffeine citrate. Pulse oximetry and arterial blood gas (ABG) monitoring are standard.

knowledge_base.title: CVICU — Hemodynamic Monitoring
knowledge_base.content: Hemodynamic monitoring in CVICU includes pulmonary artery catheter (PAC) measurements: cardiac output (CO), cardiac index (CI), systemic vascular resistance (SVR), and mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2). Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitors cerebral and somatic oxygenation. Vasoactive medications include milrinone, dobutamine, and vasopressin.

knowledge_base.title: ED — Trauma and Resuscitation
knowledge_base.content: ED trauma resuscitation follows ATLS (Advanced Trauma Life Support) protocols. Primary survey: airway, breathing, circulation, disability, exposure (ABCDE). Secondary survey follows. Damage control resuscitation (DCR) uses balanced blood products. FAST exam (Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma) detects free fluid. GCS below 8 typically indicates need for airway protection.

knowledge_base.title: ICU — Sepsis and Infection
knowledge_base.content: ICU sepsis management follows Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) bundles. SIRS criteria: temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, WBC count. Septic shock requires vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg and serum lactate >2 mmol/L. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (BSA) are initiated early. Procalcitonin (PCT) guides antibiotic de-escalation. Blood cultures (BC) are drawn before antibiotic administration.

knowledge_base.title: PICU — Neurological Assessment
knowledge_base.content: PICU neurological assessment uses the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and Pediatric GCS for younger children. Intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring may be used in traumatic brain injury (TBI). Electroencephalogram (EEG) monitors for subclinical seizures. Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) = MAP - ICP, target >50 mmHg in children. Hyperosmolar therapy with mannitol or hypertonic saline reduces cerebral edema.

knowledge_base.title: HUC — Documentation and Order Processing
knowledge_base.content: HUC documentation responsibilities include transcribing physician orders into the EMR, printing discharge instructions, coordinating dietary orders (NPO, clear liquids, etc.), scheduling imaging (CT, MRI, X-ray) and lab draws. Kardex maintenance and shift report preparation are standard duties. HUC must flag STAT orders and critical lab values (CLV) to the nurse immediately.

knowledge_base.title: ICU — Ventilator Management
knowledge_base.content: ICU ventilator management uses lung-protective ventilation: tidal volume (Vt) 6 mL/kg IBW, plateau pressure (Pplat) <30 cmH2O, and adequate PEEP. Ventilator modes include assist-control (AC), synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV), and pressure support ventilation (PSV). Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) assess readiness for extubation. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) bundles are standard of care.

knowledge_base.title: CVICU — Post-Cardiac Surgery Care
knowledge_base.content: Post-CABG care in CVICU monitors for complications: atrial fibrillation (most common arrhythmia), low cardiac output syndrome (LCOS), bleeding requiring re-exploration, and pericardial effusion. Chest tube output is closely monitored. Protamine reversal of heparin is used intraoperatively. Early mobilisation and respiratory physiotherapy reduce complications. INR and ACT guide anticoagulation management.

knowledge_base.title: NICU — Infection and Pharmacology
knowledge_base.content: NICU infection prevention includes hand hygiene, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) bundles, and cohorting of infants with RSV or other infections. Common medications: ampicillin and gentamicin for empiric sepsis coverage, fluconazole prophylaxis in VLBW infants, indomethacin or ibuprofen for patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) closure. Total daily fluid (TDF) is calculated by weight in mL/kg/day.
